subject: Genetics
title: Dreaming of a Complete Map
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dreaming of a Complete Map.

hook.text: In 1984, scientists had a wild idea: read every letter of human DNA. All 3 billion of them.

buildup.text: Biologists debated for years. Some said it was impossible. Others said it was too expensive and too slow.

discovery.text: In 1990, Congress funded the Human Genome Project. Budget: $3 billion. Deadline: 15 years. The race began.

twist.text: At launch, technology could read only 500 letters per day. They needed to read 3 billion. Math was brutal.

climax.text: It became the largest coordinated biology project in history—20 labs across 6 countries working as one.

punchline.text: They didn't know if it was possible. They started anyway.
